# decisions.json and report style

## decisions.json

Write `.git/nf-core-template-sync/decisions.json` during phase 2. `finalise.py check` validates it, and `report.py` turns it into the HTML report and the PR comment.

```json
{
  "summary": "This PR merges the nf-core/tools 4.1.0 template into the pipeline. Six files had conflicts. The agent kept all pipeline settings and took the template changes to CI and configuration. Two decisions need review.",
  "disclosure": "Generated by <agent name and model>",
  "decisions": [
    {
      "file": "conf/igenomes.config",
      "category": "combined",
      "choice": "Took the template file and added back the `bismark` keys in the new map syntax.",
      "reason": "The template changed the file to map syntax. The pipeline needs the `bismark` index paths.",
      "sources": [
        {
          "title": "Blog post for 4.1.0",
          "url": "https://nf-co.re/blog/2026/tools-4_1_0"
        }
      ],
      "nextflow_docs": [
        "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nextflow-io/nextflow/v25.10.4/docs/config.md"
      ],
      "needs_review": true
    }
  ],
  "pr_summary": {
    "kept": ["Pipeline parameters, DOI and changelog history"],
    "adopted": [
      "New `UTILS_NFSCHEMA_PLUGIN` argument",
      "Template CI workflow updates"
    ],
    "cleanups": ["Removed files that the template deleted"],
    "behaviour_changes": []
  },
  "divergence_notes": {
    "nextflow.config": "Move the pipeline parameters below the template block."
  },
  "follow_ups": [{ "title": "Short title", "detail": "One or two sentences." }]
}
```

| Field              | Rule                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `summary`          | 2 to 4 sentences: what changed and what a reviewer must examine.                                                                                    |
| `disclosure`       | The AI disclosure line that the pipeline `AGENTS.md` requires.                                                                                      |
| `decisions`        | At least one entry for each file in the worklist conflicts, and one for each non-obvious choice.                                                    |
| `category`         | `template`, `pipeline`, `combined`, `agent-written`, `deleted` or `kept` (a file that the template removed).                                        |
| `sources`          | Links that support the choice: release notes, blog post, reference PR, docs.                                                                        |
| `nextflow_docs`    | Required for new Nextflow code (see `nextflow-docs.md`).                                                                                            |
| `needs_review`     | `true` if the agent wrote new code, if sources disagree, if pipeline behaviour can change, if pipeline content was removed, or if you are not sure. |
| `pr_summary`       | Short items for the PR comment. Put changes that users of the pipeline notice in `behaviour_changes`.                                               |
| `divergence_notes` | Optional ideas to make a file closer to the template, to prevent future conflicts.                                                                  |
| `follow_ups`       | Optional extra follow-up actions. The script always adds "update all modules", nf-test and review items.                                            |

## Writing style

People who are not experts read the report and the PR comment. Use Simplified Technical English:

- Write short sentences: 20 words or fewer for instructions, 25 or fewer for descriptions.
- Write one idea in each sentence. Use the active voice and simple tenses.
- Use the same word for the same thing every time: "template", "pipeline", "sync branch", "`dev`".
- Do not use hedges ("it seems", "probably"), metaphors or rhetorical questions.
- Put file names, commands and code in backticks.
- Use British spelling (nf-core rule).

Example. Not: "We went ahead and pretty much took the template's version since it seemed to be the safer bet." Write: "The agent took the template version. The pipeline did not change this file."
